"'''Lean Back'''" is a song by American [[Hip-hop|hip hop]] group [[Terror Squad (group)|Terror Squad]]. It was released as the second single from their second studio album, ''[[True Story (album)|True Story]]'', on June 1, 2004. An uptempo [[Hip-hop|hip hop]] song built for the club environment, it contains vocal performances from group members [[Fat Joe]] and [[Remy Ma]] (credited as Remy) and production from [[Scott Storch]]. It topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for three weeks, starting on August 21, 2004, and topped the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart for seven weeks. Worldwide, the song reached the top 20 in several other countries, including Denmark, where it peaked at number five.

"Lean Back" is a song by American hip hop group Terror Squad. It was released as the second single from their second studio album, True Story, on June 1, 2004. An uptempo hip hop song built for the club environment, it contains vocal performances from group members Fat Joe and Remy Ma (credited as Remy) and production from Scott Storch. It topped the US Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks, starting on August 21, 2004, and topped the Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart for seven weeks. Worldwide, the song reached the top 20 in several other countries, including Denmark, where it peaked at number five.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Jason Birchmeier of [[AllMusic]] called "Lean Back" "a perfect club-ready duet between [[Fat Joe]] and [[Remy Ma|Remy]] that boasts a trademark [[Scott Storch]] beat and a memorable singalong hook and dance-along step".<ref>{{cite web|last=Birchmeier|first=Jason|title="True Story" - Overview|url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r703323|pure_url=yes}}|publisher=Allmusic|year=2004|accessdate=November 10, 2007}}</ref> ''[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]'' called the song a "summer classic".<ref>{{citation|last=Murphy|first=Keith|title=All for One|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yyYEAAAAMBAJ|work=Vibe|date=September 2004|volume=12|issue=9|page=190}}</ref> In 2008, the song was ranked at number 55 on [[VH1]]'s 100 Greatest Songs of [[Hip-hop|Hip Hop]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vh1.com/shows/dyn/the_greatest/140907/episode_featured_copy.jhtml|title=100 greatest hip hop songs (60-41)|publisher=VH1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081002053414/http://www.vh1.com/shows/dyn/the_greatest/140907/episode_featured_copy.jhtml|archive-date=October 2, 2008}}</ref>
sections.text: Jason Birchmeier of AllMusic called "Lean Back" "a perfect club-ready duet between Fat Joe and Remy that boasts a trademark Scott Storch beat and a memorable singalong hook and dance-along step". Vibe called the song a "summer classic". In 2008, the song was ranked at number 55 on VH1's 100 Greatest Songs of Hip Hop.

sections.heading: Remixes
sections.wikitext:
The official remixed version of the song, featuring Lil Jon, [[Eminem]], and [[Mase]] is available on Fat Joe's 2005 album ''[[All or Nothing (Fat Joe album)|All or Nothing]]'' and Lil Jon & the East Side Boyz's ''[[Crunk Juice]]'' remix disc. The official remix is more uptempo and contains a new beat with a [[crunk]]–like feel to it. However, there are two different versions of the remix. The ''All or Nothing'' version, the main remix, features an additional verse by [[Remy Ma|Remy]] and was released in July 2004.<ref>{{cite web|last=Patel|first=Joseph|title=Eminem, Mase Pitch In To Make 'Lean Back' Even Hotter|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1489616/eminem-mase-get-on-lean-back-remix.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107120519/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1489616/eminem-mase-get-on-lean-back-remix.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2012|publisher=MTV News|access-date=July 3, 2011|date=July 22, 2004}}</ref> The ''[[Crunk Juice]]'' version features Lil Jon's vocals throughout the song, omitting Remy's verse. On both versions, Mase's verse is in line with his then-clean style of rapping (as heard on his 2004 album ''[[Welcome Back (Mase album)|Welcome Back]]'').

Fat Joe also released a remix in tribute to his [[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] ancestry, featuring [[Tego Calderón]] and [[Tony Touch]]. Other remixes of the song are performed by [[Chamillionaire]], on ''[[The Mixtape Messiah]]'' titled "Body Rock", [[Lil Wayne]], [[Max B]], [[Jadakiss]], [[U.S.D.A (band)|U.S.D.A.]], and [[G-Unit]]. Also, [[Mashup (music)|mashup]] artist [[Girl Talk (musician)|Girl Talk]] layered "Lean Back" over [[Spacehog]]'s "[[In the Meantime (Spacehog song)|In the Meantime]]" in his 2010 album ''[[All Day (Girl Talk album)|All Day]]''. [[Houston]] rapper [[Lil' Flip]] did a freestyle over the song as a diss towards [[Atlanta]] rapper [[T.I.]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.songtextemania.com/lean_back_freestyle_ti_diss_songtext_lil_flip.html | title=Lean Back Freestyle (T.i. Diss) | publisher=SongTextMania.com | access-date=July 2, 2013 | author=Lil Flip}}</ref>
sections.text:
The official remixed version of the song, featuring Lil Jon, Eminem, and Mase is available on Fat Joe's 2005 album All or Nothing and Lil Jon & the East Side Boyz's Crunk Juice remix disc. The official remix is more uptempo and contains a new beat with a crunk–like feel to it. However, there are two different versions of the remix. The All or Nothing version, the main remix, features an additional verse by Remy and was released in July 2004. The Crunk Juice version features Lil Jon's vocals throughout the song, omitting Remy's verse. On both versions, Mase's verse is in line with his then-clean style of rapping (as heard on his 2004 album Welcome Back).

Fat Joe also released a remix in tribute to his Puerto Rican ancestry, featuring Tego Calderón and Tony Touch. Other remixes of the song are performed by Chamillionaire, on The Mixtape Messiah titled "Body Rock", Lil Wayne, Max B, Jadakiss, U.S.D.A., and G-Unit. Also, mashup artist Girl Talk layered "Lean Back" over Spacehog's "In the Meantime" in his 2010 album All Day. Houston rapper Lil' Flip did a freestyle over the song as a diss towards Atlanta rapper T.I.
